title: CYBRIK resource-bounds common definitions v1
description: Shared accounting-only primitives for conserved resource bounds across a call tree. cybrik.res-* is disjoint from the accepted investigation budget object, budget_exceeded, BUDGET_*, over_input_budget, over_output_budget, and fallbackInfo.reason=budget; this proposal maps, renames, extends, or replaces none of them. A res identifier is never a credential, capability, permission, delegation, or approval. Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION — NOT IMPLEMENTED, v0.1.0; not stable v1/GA and not a bundle tag. Gate W2-H, ADR-0012.

closureReason.description: One terminal accounting-closure vocabulary, hoisted here so the release reason and the root-closure reason cannot drift apart.

idempotencyKey.description: Accounting replay key only. It confers no authority.

orgScopeRef.description: Opaque advisory org-scope hint aligned with accepted W1-C2. Authoritative scope derives from authenticated policy; this copy introduces no W1-C2 mutation.

resourceVector.description: Fixed additive vector of conserved credits. Deadline and peak memory are deliberately absent because they are not conserved credits.

parentRef.description: Accounting lineage only. A parent reference never confers permission.

rootRef.description: Identity of the root grant whose tree this record belongs to. Accounting lineage only: naming a root grant is not possession of it and confers no credential, capability, permission, delegation, approval, or capacity. There is deliberately no expected_version here — a root binding is an identity statement, not a compare-and-set against root state, and adding one would create a second concurrency axis.

virtualTimeMs.description: Fixture-supplied logical time; never a wall-clock claim.

ledgerSequence.description: Dense accounting sequence within one root tree: sequences start at 1 and increase by exactly 1, with no gap, no repeat, and no reordering; a violation is RES_SEQUENCE_VIOLATION. A dense sequence from 1 means exactly one serialization point per root tree, so v0.1 admits no concurrent independent writers within one root and no partitioned or per-branch sub-sequences. This is a contract-level limit and makes no throughput, scaling, or runtime-concurrency claim. Density is a cross-record property that a single-record schema cannot express, so the numeric constraint here is only integer, minimum 1.

confersAuthority.description: Load-bearing denial of credential, capability, permission, delegation, and approval semantics.
